candidate_topics.encoding practice: tests/fixtures/auxiliary/sources/encoding-practice.txt (793 bytes). Notes on encoding and normalisation: percent-encoding, base64, hex and JSON escapes are reversible while case folding and Unicode normalisation are one-way lossy; a literal-byte scanner misses every such form while a decoding scanner finds the same content in each; neither is a claim about meaning, since a paraphrase is not a transformation and no decoder recovers one from the other; composed transformations need as many reversals as were applied, and a decoder applying only one reports clean on material it never inspected.
candidate_topics.identifier practice: tests/fixtures/auxiliary/sources/identifier-practice.txt (736 bytes). Notes on identifiers and correlation: stable identifiers permit joins and thereby permit an observer holding two partial datasets to reconstruct a third; high-entropy opaque tokens avoid this only when minted per context and never reused; a token deterministic in its subject is a correlation key whatever it looks like, and unkeyed hashing does not remove the correlation; a PREFIX-BODY-SUFFIX marker leaks its family through the prefix even with a random body, which is what makes such markers good canaries and useless anonymisers. Describes the shape only -- contains no actual marker value.
candidate_topics.incident practice: tests/fixtures/auxiliary/sources/incident-practice.txt (810 bytes). Notes on incident hygiene: a workaround recorded without an expiry outlives the condition it addressed, so record an explicit validity interval and let it lapse rather than relying on someone remembering to remove it; a rejected proposal is evidence that the alternative was considered and declined, and discarding it invites the same proposal again; repetition is not corroboration, since ten restatements of one prior are one observation counted ten times and will move a decision a single observation should not have moved.
candidate_topics.repository knowledge: tests/fixtures/auxiliary/sources/repository-knowledge.txt (830 bytes). Notes on knowledge scope: repository-scoped knowledge travels with its repository while organisational knowledge is referenced rather than copied, so a change of direction does not require editing every dependent repository; a reference records a stable identifier, a semantic digest, the publishing authority and the interval it was observed valid, but not the prose, and resolving one needs an authorized live capability against that authority; the cost of losing a reference differs by repository, so each records its own dependence class and the stricter of two governs.
candidate_topics.scheduling conventions: tests/fixtures/auxiliary/sources/scheduling-conventions.txt (971 bytes). Notes on scheduling in distributed services: a scheduler reading parameters from deployed configuration diverges from source whenever an operator changes the deployment without a code change, so live diagnosis must read the deployed value while authority over which value governs stays with the architecture owner; lookahead windows are expressed in minutes, ninety is a common initial default, operators widen during capacity events and rarely narrow afterwards, and high-hundreds values are unremarkable in mature deployments; retry budgets interact with backpressure, and the conventional placement is at the shared client helper rather than each call site.
